text:
chris: Quick heads-up — we're onboarding a new APAC account for Dedicated GPU pools (ap-southeast-1). Before we flip the switch I want to request IP/ENI/EIP headroom so we don't hit quotas during canary + scale. Timeline: canary next Wed, full pool in ~3 weeks.

irina: numbers? what exact quotas do you want us to ask for?

chris: initial pool = 120 GPU nodes (A100 equiv) across 3 AZs (40 nodes/AZ). Our node setup uses 1 primary ENI per instance and we rely on secondary private IPs for pods. Expected secondary IPs: ~8 per node for ephemeral GPU pods. So rough needs:
- assignable private IPv4 addresses: 120 * (1+8) = 1,080 (+20% buffer => ~1,300)
- ENIs: nodes + infra = ~140, request ENI per VPC increased to 2,000 to be safe
- Elastic IPs: plan to have NAT pools + some public-assigned ephemeral workloads, request 600 EIPs (we use 3 NAT gateways initially + burstable public IPs)
- IPv6: request a /56 VPC IPv6 pool (or be able to request subnet /64s) so we can enable native IPv6 for pods and avoid exhausting v4 addresses

maria: 600 EIPs is large — AWS charge applies. Are we planning to assign EIPs per-pod or only NAT EIPs + few public?

chris: Mostly NAT EIPs + a small number of externally-addressable jobs. The 600 is a conservative headroom number for bursts and canary; we can reduce to 400 if cost team pushes back. Primary blocker is lack of assignable IPv4 addresses in the account plus default ENI ceilings.

alex: For mitigation we could:
- allocate a secondary IPv4 CIDR to the VPC (if account/region allows) to get more private IPs
- enable IPv6-only paths for pods and NAT64 for the minority of IPv4-only endpoints
- use a small fleet of EC2 instances as jumpers with ephemeral public IPs instead of allocating EIPs to many pods
Would prefer allocating a secondary CIDR + IPv6 /56.

chris: Good call. I've included the secondary CIDR option in the ask. For rollout we want both: extra IPv4 headroom + IPv6 so apps can drift to v6 over time.

sam: Can you paste the exact wording you want me to open with AWS? I'll open the support case and escalate to account team.

chris: Please use this template: 

```
Account: 123456789012 (new-apac-prod)
Region: ap-southeast-1
Request: Increase per-VPC ENI limit to 2000, increase Elastic IP quota to 600, enable allocation of a secondary RFC1918 IPv4 CIDR for VPCs, and assign a /56 IPv6 pool or allow subnet /64 delegations. Purpose: Dedicated GPU pool rollout (canary next Wed) — 120 nodes initially, expected 1,300 assignable private IPv4 addresses and 3 NAT gateways. Please expedite — tagging this as business-critical for production rollout.
```

chris: Also ask for a soft quota increase on NAT gateway per-region and for ELB quotas (we may attach ALBs per AZ).

aws-support-bot: Support case created: AWSSUP-87654321. Initial response ETA 24h. 

irina: Thanks. I'll ping account manager directly and add cost + security owners to the thread. @maria can you confirm whether 400 EIPs would be acceptable from cost?

maria: 400 is palatable if we commit to aggressive IPv6 migration within 6 weeks. Approve provisional 400.

chris: OK lowering EIP ask to 400 in the ticket, but still request ENI->2000 + secondary CIDR + /56 IPv6. 

sam: Opened ticket AWSSUP-87654321 with EIP=400, ENI=2000, secondary CIDR request, /56 IPv6. Escalated to TAM. Pushing for <12h response.

alex: For immediate canary, add temporary workaround doc: use per-AZ small NAT fleet with autoscaling and shared EIPs to limit allocations. I'll draft and drop in #eng-infra-runbooks.

chris: Awesome. Action items:
- sam: follow up AWSSUP-87654321 and paste updates here
- alex: runbook for NAT + shared EIP pattern (canary only)
- irina: liaise with account manager on secondary CIDR approval
- maria: confirm final cost approval for 400 EIPs

sam: noted, will update thread when I hear back from TAM. :thumbsup:

maria: approve provisional cost for 400 EIPs, please track burn.

chris: thanks team — will hold canary until we have either the AWS confirmation or the NAT-runbook mitigations in place. :white_check_mark:
